entries.zh_title: deconbatch：事故编程法，或余项如何自己写代码
entries.en_title: deconbatch: The Accidental Programming Method, or How the Remainder Writes Its Own Code
entries.notes: Anonymous Japanese creative coder who runs 'Land of 1000 Creative Codings' blog. Proposed the Accidental Programming Method: change parameters thoughtlessly, swap operators, treat bugs as discoveries. De Jong attractor jellyfish shapes found by hand-tuning. Perlin noise bug produced superior aesthetics. All code open source. No gallery/NFT/curatorial presence. The method itself is a remainder-production mechanism.

entries.zh_title: LB Allix：从氰版到绘图仪，余项的迁徙
entries.en_title: LB Allix: From Cyanotype to Plotter, the Migration of the Remainder
entries.notes: Paris-based artist who moved from cyanotype photography to pen plotter generative art. The entry focuses on how chemical contingency migrates into algorithmic contingency, and how daily practice itself is a structural remainder. Architecture and spatial design background gives her a non-programmer approach to generative line work.

entries.en_title: Landlines Art: After the Code Misfires
entries.notes: Generative artist driven by accidental coding mistakes. Key work: Sedimentary Dissolution (512 pieces, interactive erosion algorithms). Featured at The Generative Art Museum (TGAM). Collectors can manipulate works via keystroke — completion itself stays open.
